title: Voltage, current, resistance, and safety

spans.text: Voltage pushes charge, current measures its flow, and resistance limits that flow. Voltage is measured in volts, current in amperes, and resistance in ohms. A closed circuit provides a complete path from the source through the load and back.
Ohm's law: V = I × R. A 5 V source across 1 kΩ gives about 5 mA. In a simple DC circuit, power is P = V × I; a load that exceeds a board pin's limits must not be powered directly from that pin.
